requirements.ask_text: Could you tell me your phone last4?

source.text: `phone_last4` — ask for your phone last4. Format digits, exactly 6 digits including leading zeros.

requirements.ask_text: Could you tell me your date of birth?
requirements.hint_reply: Could you say your date of birth again: day, then month, then year?

source.text: `date_of_birth` — ask for your date of birth. Format date, sent as YYYY-MM-DD; a date given only as numbers is read day, then month, then year.

requirements.ask_text: Could you tell me your postcode?

source.text: `postcode` — ask for your postcode. Format text: letters and digits, spaces removed.

requirements.ask_text: Could you tell me your birth year?

source.text: `birth_year` — ask for your birth year. Format year, four digits.

identity.failed_instruction: Please use the mobile app or visit a branch.

source.text: A wrong answer may be asked again. 5 wrong answers in total end the check, whichever question they were on; the API's `wrong_answers_left` is the count to use. ... Ask once more; if it is still unclear after the second ask, close as `not_reached` / `unclear`. ... A second refusal closes as `not_verified` / `declined`.

A callback is for the next business day only, never today, from 09:00 to 17:30, both included, and later than `now`. ... If the person names a time outside that window, say so and ask once more. If no valid time results, close as `not_reached` / `no_callback`.

third_party.deceased_sentence: I am sorry for your loss.

source.text: Wrong number: apologise and close as `not_reached` / `wrong_number`. The customer has died: say "I am sorry for your loss." and close as `not_reached` / `deceased`.

Business days are Monday to Saturday, except Bank 9 holidays: 2026-10-14, 2026-10-15. "Next <weekday>" means that weekday of the following week, even when today is that weekday; "this <weekday>" means the coming one.

| 1 to 90 | band1 | the last business day of the current calendar month | 1 | ... Attempt 1: propose the full past-due amount on the last business day of this week; if today is that day, the last business day of next week. If the customer already said the full amount is too much, attempt 1 proposes the floor instead.

Ask for the full past-due amount first. Never ask "how much can you pay?". Any amount between the floor and the full amount is accepted; an amount below the floor is refused, and the floor is offered once per product with the words "the rest stays overdue".

A promise date must be today or later, a business day, and not after the deadline. A weekend day or holiday rolls to the next business day. A vague date (next week, when I get paid): ask once for the exact day; if none follows, propose the deadline. A date after the deadline: offer the deadline instead.

special_cases.name: already_paid
special_cases.trigger: The customer says they have already paid.
special_cases.say: Payments can take one business day to appear.

source.text: Already paid: say "Payments can take one business day to appear.". Close as `paid`.

special_cases.name: dispute
special_cases.trigger: The customer disputes the debt: it is not their debt, they never had the product, or it was closed or paid off before.

source.text: Dispute (not their debt, never had the product, closed or paid off before): close as `no_promise` / `dispute`.

special_cases.name: hardship
special_cases.trigger: The customer mentions hardship such as illness, a death in the family, or job loss.
special_cases.say: I am sorry to hear that.

source.text: Hardship (illness, a death in the family, job loss): say one short sentence of sympathy, make no persuasion attempt, and offer a transfer to the `support` team. If they accept, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `support` and close as `transferred` / `support`. If they decline, close as `no_promise` / `hardship`. A customer in hardship may still name a date and amount; record it.

special_cases.name: restructuring
special_cases.trigger: The customer asks for a payment plan, lower instalments, or changing the terms.

source.text: Restructuring (a payment plan, lower instalments, changing the terms): call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `restructuring` and close as `transferred` / `restructuring`. Promises already recorded on this call stay recorded.

special_cases.name: human
special_cases.trigger: The customer asks to speak to a human agent (during the identity check or after verification).

source.text: A request for a human agent during the identity check: ask once whether you can help first; if they insist, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `general` and close as `transferred` / `human`. ... A request for a human after verification: ask once whether you can help first; if they insist, transfer to `general` and close as `transferred` / `human`.

special_cases.name: scam
special_cases.trigger: The person suspects the call is a scam.
special_cases.say: You can verify this call by phoning Bank 9's customer service number.

source.text: If the person suspects a scam: say they can verify the call by phoning Bank 9's customer service number, and continue.

special_cases.name: robot
special_cases.trigger: The person asks whether this is a robot.

source.text: If asked whether this is a robot: say "I am Bank 9's digital assistant."
The customer refuses to talk: close as `no_promise` / `refused`.

special_cases.name: change_promise
special_cases.trigger: The customer asks whether a recorded promise can be changed.
special_cases.say: You can change it in the mobile app.

source.text: If the customer asks whether a recorded promise can be changed: say "You can change it in the mobile app."

table.when: A transfer, with the transfer's reason, even after a promise.
No promise; reason of the first product in get_account order that is not paid.

source.text: Thank the customer and say goodbye before `close_call`, which is the last tool call. ... At least one promise recorded: `promise`. A transfer: `transferred` with the transfer's reason, even after a promise. All products already paid: `paid`. No promise: `no_promise` with the reason of the first product in `get_account` order that is not paid.
`add_note` is never used.

`get_account` returns up to 3 products. ... Every product is handled on the same call: a common date is checked against each product's own deadline and clamped to it; one read-back covers all pending promises; a transfer after a recorded promise keeps the promise.

phrases.opening: I am the automated assistant of Bank 9, and this call is recorded.
phrases.debt_intro: I am calling from the Bank 9 collections team about a late payment.
phrases.today_question: Can you pay all of it today?
phrases.all_today_question: Can you pay all of it today?
phrases.scam_reply: You can verify this call by phoning Bank 9's customer service number.
phrases.after_promise_sentence: You will receive a text message confirming this promise.
phrases.already_paid_sentence: Payments can take one business day to appear.
phrases.recorded_promise_change_reply: You can change it in the mobile app.

source.text: First sentence: say you are the automated assistant of Bank 9 and that the call is recorded. Then ask whether you are speaking with the customer, using title and last name. ... After verification say you are calling from the Bank 9 collections team about a late payment. ... then ask once whether they can pay all of it today. ... `business_overdraft` (say "business overdraft") ... `equipment_loan` (say "equipment loan")
If `create_promise` fails, try once more; if it still fails, say you could not record it and close as `no_promise` / `service_error`.

The API can return hint 'day_month_swapped' for date_of_birth, but the brief does not say what to reply or whether the hint counts as a wrong answer; a short re-ask in day-month-year order was used.
The brief gives no sentence for questions the agent cannot answer.
The brief requires 'one short sentence of sympathy' but does not dictate its words.
